judgements.justification: B's AC shared K4dB's overclaiming concern and said only that the work 'may be enough for justifying publication', yet B gave a spotlight with no stated case.

Only A's reviewers named the hidden tree Markov model, latent tree and factor graph grammar literature and doubted the self-made baseline, while B's gxvj and VzMU took the reported comparisons at face value.
A's AC cited the unanimous below-threshold scores correctly; it added its own novelty view but did not misstate any reviewer's final position.
k7kf's 'very narrow domain' point concerns the single test domain, not the paper's audience, and B's 1oXa also doubted real-world applications, so breadth did not split the committees.
B's detractor K4dB read the paper correctly and the paper confirms its concern; no misreading detractor shaped either meta-review.
The authors added no experiments on either forum.
In both committees the high-confidence reviewers rated in line with their committee's outcome (A's c2bx 4 at confidence 4; B's gxvj and 1oXa 7 and 8 at confidence 4).
No reviewer added a new objection and cut a score after the response period; c2bx raised its score and uEGL kept its 5.

B's 1oXa rated 8 while doubting any important application and saying a simpler method could do the same, while A's k7kf called the paper a 'Good contribution' and rated 4 and c2bx called the model well founded and rated 4.
The overclaiming concern came from B's K4dB and AC, yet B gave the higher tier, so the concern did not cap the tier.
No committee converged on flat marginal-accept ratings: A rated 4, 4, 4, 5 and B rated 8, 7, 6, 5.
